title: Prevention of Steep Slope Disasters Act
full_text:
Chapter 1 General Provisions

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to protect the lives and property of the people from the risk of the collapse of steep slopes and other such hazards and to contribute to the promotion of public welfare by providing for the designation and management of areas at risk of steep-slope collapse, the formulation and implementation of improvement plans, emergency measures, and other related matters.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows. <Amended 2008.12.29, 2012.12.18, 2015.1.20, 2016.5.29, 2017.3.21, 2018.10.16, 2020.6.9>
1. "Steep slope" means a natural slope or artificial slope (including retaining walls, embankment walls, and the like; hereinafter the same shall apply) forming part of housing sites, roads, railways, park facilities, or similar facilities, or mountainous land adjacent thereto, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
2. "Collapse risk area" means a steep slope and its surrounding land where collapse, falling rocks, or similar events may cause harm to the lives or property of the people and which have been designated and publicly notified pursuant to Article 6.
3. "Disaster" means damage occurring on a steep slope due to a natural disaster under subparagraph 1(a) of Article 3 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety.
4. "Disaster risk assessment" means the quantitative and qualitative analysis and prediction of risk by a person with experience and technical expertise through visual inspections or inspections using instruments or other means, in order to analyze social and geographical conditions, collapse risk factors, the anticipated scale of damage, the history of disasters, and other matters relating to the collapse of a steep slope or similar events.
5. "Managing agency" means any of the following administrative agencies and public institutions that own or manage a steep slope:
(a) A local government;
(b) A regional forest service;
(c) The Korea Rural Community Corporation under the Korea Rural Community Corporation and Farmland Management Fund Act;
(d) The Korea Land and Housing Corporation under the Korea Land and Housing Corporation Act;
(e) Deleted <2012.12.18>
(f) The Korea National Railway under the Korea National Railway Act;
(g) An urban railroad corporation under the Urban Railroad Act;
(h) The Korea National Park Service under the Korea National Park Service Act;
(i) Any other administrative agency or public institution prescribed by Presidential Decree.
6. "Instrumentation business" means the business of continuously taking measurements of steep slopes subject to this Act and other facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 3 (Scope of Application) This Act shall not apply to express national highways under Article 11 of the Road Act, general national highways under Article 12 of that Act, or facilities under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Special Act on the Safety Control and Maintenance of Establishments. <Amended 2008.3.21, 2014.1.14, 2017.1.17>

Article 4 (Relationship to Other Acts) This Act shall take precedence over other Acts with regard to the designation and management of steep slopes, emergency measures, and other related matters.

Chapter 2 Designation and Management of Collapse Risk Areas

Article 5 (Safety Inspections of Steep Slopes)
① A managing agency shall conduct safety inspections of the steep slopes under its jurisdiction at least 2 times a year and notify the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, the mayor of a Si (including an administrative mayor under Article 11(1) of the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province and the Development of Free International City; hereinafter the same shall apply), the head of a Gun, or the head of a Gu (meaning the head of an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply) of the results. <Amended 2017.3.21>
② A managing agency shall disclose the results of the safety inspections under paragraph 1 through its website. <Newly inserted 2020.10.20>
③ The scope of the safety inspection results to be disclosed pursuant to paragraph 2, the period of disclosure, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly inserted 2020.10.20>
④ A Special Self-Governing City Mayor, the mayor of a Si, the head of a Gun, or the head of a Gu (hereinafter referred to as the "head of a Si/Gun/Gu") shall conduct safety inspections of steep slopes within the area under his or her jurisdiction at least 1 time a year: Provided, That safety inspections may be omitted for a steep slope which, upon receipt of notification of the results under paragraph 1, is determined to present no risk of collapse. <Amended 2017.3.21, 2020.10.20>
⑤ The head of a Si/Gun/Gu may, where necessary to improve the efficiency of the safety inspections under paragraph 4, conduct them jointly with relevant agencies and experts. <Amended 2017.3.21, 2020.10.20>
⑥ The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall notify the relevant managing agency and the owner, occupant, or manager of the land concerned (hereinafter referred to as an "interested person") of the results of the inspections under paragraphs 4 and 5, so that they take the measures necessary for safety. <Amended 2017.3.21, 2020.10.20>

Article 5-2 (Surveys of the Actual Conditions of Steep Slopes)
① The Minister of the Interior and Safety or a Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor/Do Governor") may conduct a survey of actual conditions to ascertain the current state of steep slopes. In such cases, the results shall be notified to the heads of Si/Gun/Gu and the managing agencies.
② Where a steep slope is newly identified as a result of a survey of actual conditions under paragraph 1, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu and the managing agency shall manage the steep slope in accordance with this Act, unless there is a special reason not to do so.
③ Matters necessary for the scope and methods of the surveys of actual conditions under paragraph 1 and other related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Designation of Collapse Risk Areas)
① Where, after conducting a safety inspection under Article 5 of a steep slope under its jurisdiction, a managing agency finds it necessary to designate the slope as a collapse risk area, it shall conduct a disaster risk assessment and complete procedures for obtaining residents' opinions, and then request the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the area to designate it as a collapse risk area. Upon receiving the request, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall immediately designate and publicly notify the area, unless there is a special reason not to do so. The same shall apply to any change thereto. <Amended 2015.1.20, 2017.3.21>
② The head of a Si/Gun/Gu may directly conduct a disaster risk assessment of a steep slope within the area under his or her jurisdiction that is owned or managed by a person other than a managing agency, complete procedures for obtaining residents' opinions, and designate and publicly notify it as a collapse risk area. In such cases, the relevant head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall become the managing agency for that collapse risk area.
③ Where a managing agency so requests in relation to the designation of a collapse risk area under paragraph 1, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu may obtain residents' opinions.
④ When the head of a Si/Gun/Gu has designated and publicly notified a collapse risk area pursuant to paragraph 1 or 2, he or she shall inform the interested persons of that fact: Provided, That where the address or residence of an interested person is unclear, public notice as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety shall substitute for such notification. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
⑤ Where a steep slope has been designated and publicly notified as a natural disaster risk improvement district pursuant to Article 12 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act, it shall be deemed to have been designated and publicly notified as a collapse risk area pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2. <Amended 2012.10.22>
⑥ Matters concerning the methods and procedures for disaster risk assessments under paragraphs 1 and 2 and the procedures for obtaining residents' opinions shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree, and other matters necessary for the designation, public notification, and alteration of collapse risk areas shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
⑦ Where the risk of disaster has been eliminated through the implementation of a collapse risk area improvement project or by other means, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall obtain the opinions of relevant experts, cancel the designation of the collapse risk area, and publicly notify the result. <Newly inserted 2015.1.20>

Article 6-2 (Recommendations to Designate Collapse Risk Areas)
① Where the head of a Si/Gun/Gu does not designate a steep slope under his or her jurisdiction that poses a high risk of collapse as a collapse risk area pursuant to Article 6(1) and (2), the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, a Do Governor, or a Special Self-Governing Province Governor may recommend that the head of the Si/Gun/Gu designate and publicly notify the area as a collapse risk area. In such cases, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall comply, unless there is a special reason not to do so. <Amended 2017.3.21, 2017.7.26>
② Where a managing agency does not request designation as a collapse risk area of a steep slope under its jurisdiction that poses a high risk of collapse pursuant to Article 6(1), the head of the Si/Gun/Gu may recommend that the managing agency request designation of the area as a collapse risk area. In such cases, the managing agency shall comply, unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 7 (Conduct of On-Site Investigations)
① Where the head of a managing agency considers it necessary for a request for designation as a collapse risk area under Article 6(1), or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu considers it necessary for the designation and public notification of a collapse risk area under paragraph 2 of that Article, he or she may have an on-site investigation team comprising staff members, experts on steep slopes, and other relevant persons conduct an on-site investigation. <Amended 2015.1.20>
② A person conducting an on-site investigation pursuant to paragraph 1 may, where necessary, enter another person's land, temporarily use such land, or alter or remove trees, soil, rocks, or other obstacles.
③ A person entering another person's land or temporarily using such land pursuant to paragraph 2, or intending to alter or remove obstacles pursuant to that paragraph, shall obtain the consent of the interested persons as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety: Provided, That where consent cannot be obtained because an interested person's address or residence is unclear, permission shall be obtained from the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
④ A person entering another person's land or temporarily using such land pursuant to paragraph 2, or intending to alter or remove obstacles pursuant to that paragraph, shall carry identification indicating his or her authority and present it to the interested persons.
⑤ Compensation for losses arising pursuant to paragraph 2 shall be governed by the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects.

Article 8 (Instrumentation Management of Steep Slopes)
① Where a managing agency or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu considers it necessary in order to detect in advance changes in position due to subsidence, sliding, toppling, collapse, or other movement of the ground of a steep slope, it may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, directly undertake continuous measurement and data management (hereinafter referred to as "continuous instrumentation management"), or have a person registered for the instrumentation business under Article 22 perform such work on its behalf. <Amended 2024.2.13>
② Where a managing agency directly undertakes continuous instrumentation management pursuant to paragraph 1 or has it undertaken on its behalf, it shall provide the measurement data in real time to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction. <Amended 2017.3.21>
③ The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall use the measurement data provided pursuant to paragraph 2 and his or her own measurement data to evacuate residents of the relevant area promptly when an emergency arises. <Amended 2017.3.21>
④ No person shall damage the instruments, equipment, or other items installed for continuous instrumentation management.
⑤ Where a managing agency or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu undertakes continuous instrumentation management pursuant to paragraph 1, the State may subsidize part of the cost of installing measurement instruments. <Newly inserted 2015.1.20, 2024.2.13>

Article 9 (Establishment and Operation of Management Standards for Evacuation of Residents)
① The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall establish and operate management standards for the evacuation of residents, taking into account the results of continuous instrumentation management, rainfall, the properties of the slopes, and other relevant factors.
② The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall, after consultation with the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies, prepare guidelines for the establishment and operation of the management standards under paragraph 1, notify the heads of Si/Gun/Gu thereof, and guide and supervise their implementation. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 10 (Consultation on Activities in Collapse Risk Areas)
① Where a relevant administrative agency intends to grant permission, authorization, a license, approval, release, a decision, consent, consultation, or the like (hereinafter referred to as "permits, authorizations, etc.") involving any of the following activities in a collapse risk area, it shall consult with the managing agency having jurisdiction in advance: Provided, That this shall not apply where consultation on disaster impact assessments, etc. has been conducted pursuant to Article 4 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act. <Amended 2017.10.24>
1. Installation of pipelines, steel towers, roads, bridges, or other structures involving excavation of soil or stone;
2. Construction, extension, or reconstruction of buildings involving excavation of soil or stone;
3. Alteration of retaining walls, embankment walls, side ditches, or similar structures;
4. Felling of trees or removal of turf or the like;
5. Other activities prescribed by Presidential Decree that impair the stability of a steep slope.
② Where a relevant administrative agency intends to undertake consultation under paragraph 1, it shall request consultation together with the documents prescribed by Presidential Decree, and the managing agency receiving the request shall notify the relevant administrative agency of the outcome of the consultation.
③ Upon receiving notification of the outcome of consultation pursuant to paragraph 2, the relevant administrative agency shall take the measures necessary to incorporate that outcome, unless there is a special reason not to do so, and shall notify the managing agency of the measures taken or plans for subsequent measures.
④ Where the outcome of consultation has been incorporated into the relevant administrative plan or development project pursuant to paragraph 3, the relevant administrative agency and the relevant project operator shall faithfully implement it.
⑤ To ensure implementation of the outcome of consultation under paragraph 4, the managing agency may request the relevant administrative agency and project operator to take necessary measures, such as suspending construction. In such cases, the relevant administrative agency and project operator shall comply, unless there is a special reason not to do so.
⑥ A relevant administrative agency shall not grant permits, authorizations, etc. before the consultation procedures under paragraph 1 have been completed.

Article 11 (Installation of Hazard Signs)
① A managing agency shall install signs warning of danger in collapse risk areas.
② Details concerning the size, information to be displayed, and other matters relating to the hazard signs installed in collapse risk areas pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
③ No person shall move or damage a hazard sign without the permission of the person who installed it pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2.

Chapter 3 Formulation and Implementation of Improvement Plans for Collapse Risk Areas

Article 12 (Formulation of Medium-Term Plans for Improvement of Collapse Risk Areas)
① A managing agency shall formulate a medium-term plan for the improvement of collapse risk areas for each 5-year period (hereinafter referred to as a "medium-term plan"), as prescribed by Presidential Decree, and notify the head of the Si/Gun/Gu thereof. The head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall submit the plan to the Minister of the Interior and Safety through the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, the Metropolitan City Mayor, the Do Governor, or the Special Self-Governing Province Governor: Provided, That the Special Self-Governing City Mayor shall submit a medium-term plan notified by a managing agency directly to the Minister of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2013.8.6, 2015.1.20, 2017.3.21, 2017.7.26>
② Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems it necessary with respect to a medium-term plan submitted pursuant to paragraph 1, the Minister may require the plan to be revised or supplemented, and the managing agency receiving such a request shall comply, unless there is a special reason not to do so. <Amended 2013.8.6, 2017.3.21, 2017.7.26>
③ In formulating a medium-term plan pursuant to paragraph 1, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may formulate relocation measures after completing procedures such as obtaining residents' opinions and conducting an economic feasibility analysis, if he or she determines that a steep-slope improvement project would require an excessive budget or that improvement of the steep slope alone would make it difficult to eliminate the fundamental causes of the risk of collapse.
④ Article 78 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects shall apply mutatis mutandis to the formulation of relocation measures under paragraph 3.

Article 13 (Implementation Plans for Improvement Projects for Collapse Risk Areas)
① A managing agency shall, on the basis of the medium-term plan formulated under Article 12, formulate and publicly notify an annual implementation plan for improvement projects after consultation with the heads of the relevant administrative agencies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. The same shall apply to any change thereto.
② When formulating an implementation plan for an improvement project pursuant to paragraph 1, a managing agency may include a project to prevent damage in an area adjacent to the collapse risk area where runoff of soil, rocks, or the like, landslides, or similar events from that adjacent area may cause damage to the collapse risk area. <Amended 2019.12.10>
③ Unless there is a special reason not to do so, a managing agency shall take the measures necessary to incorporate matters on which it has consulted with the heads of the relevant administrative agencies pursuant to paragraph 1, and shall notify those heads of the measures taken or plans for future measures.
④ A managing agency shall submit the implementation plan for an improvement project formulated pursuant to paragraph 1 to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction, and the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall submit it to the Minister of the Interior and Safety through the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, the Metropolitan City Mayor, the Do Governor, or the Special Self-Governing Province Governor: Provided, That the Special Self-Governing City Mayor shall submit an implementation plan for an improvement project submitted by a managing agency directly to the Minister of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2013.8.6, 2017.3.21, 2017.7.26>
⑤ Where the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, a Do Governor, a Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu has formulated an implementation plan for an improvement project for a collapse risk area, all or part of the costs of the improvement project may be subsidized from the National Treasury pursuant to Article 70 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act. <Amended 2015.1.20, 2017.3.21>
⑥ The Minister of the Interior and Safety may ascertain the results of implementation of the improvement project implementation plans under paragraph 1, conduct evaluations of the agencies, and confer awards. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 13-2 (Standards for Improvement Projects for Collapse Risk Areas) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall establish and publicly notify the standards necessary for investigation, planning, design, construction, and other activities relating to improvement projects for collapse risk areas in order to ensure the quality and safety of such projects and to promote advances in the relevant technologies.

Article 14 (Deeming of Permits, Authorizations, etc. under Other Acts) Where, in formulating an implementation plan for an improvement project for a collapse risk area under Article 13(1), a managing agency has consulted in advance with the heads of the relevant administrative agencies concerning any of the following permits, authorizations, etc., the relevant permits, authorizations, etc. shall be deemed to have been granted when the implementation plan for the improvement project is publicly notified, and public notification or public announcement of the permits, authorizations, etc. under the relevant Acts shall be deemed to have been made. <Amended 2008.3.21, 2010.4.15, 2014.1.14, 2019.12.10, 2022.12.27>
1. Permission for development activities under Article 56 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act;
2. Occupation and use of a road under Article 61 of the Road Act;
3. Permission to occupy and use public waters under Article 8 of the Public Waters Management and Reclamation Act, and a license to reclaim public waters under Article 28 of that Act;
4. Deleted <2010.4.15>
5. Permission for and consultation on the diversion of farmland under Article 34 of the Farmland Act, and permission for temporary use of farmland for other purposes and the like under Article 36 of that Act;
6. Diversion of grassland and other activities under Article 23 of the Grassland Act;
7. Permission for conversion of mountainous districts under Article 14 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, permission to collect soil or stone and the like under Article 25 of that Act, and permission for and reporting on the felling of standing trees and other such activities under Article 36(1) and (5) of the Creation and Management of Forest Resources Act;
8. Restrictions on activities in erosion control areas under Article 14 of the Erosion Control Work Act.

Chapter 4 Measures in Collapse Risk Areas

Article 15 (Ensuring Safety in Collapse Risk Areas)
① Any of the following interested persons notified of the designation of a collapse risk area pursuant to Article 6(4) shall conduct their own safety inspections to eliminate the risk of collapse and shall ensure the stability of the steep slope by taking necessary measures, such as emergency action, repairs, and reinforcement. <Amended 2015.8.11>
1. A management entity or other relevant person under Article 2(1)10 of the Multi-Family Housing Management Act;
2. A management authority, management corporation, or other relevant person under Articles 30 and 31 of the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act.
② The interested persons referred to in paragraph 1 shall endeavor to prevent disasters by securing the funds necessary for maintenance and management and taking other measures to ensure safety in collapse risk areas.

Article 16 (Expropriation or Use of Land)
① A managing agency may expropriate or use land, objects, or rights within a project area (hereinafter referred to as "land, etc.") where it considers this necessary to implement an improvement project for a collapse risk area pursuant to Article 13.
② When an implementation plan for an improvement project for a collapse risk area has been publicly notified pursuant to Article 13, project recognition and public notification of project recognition under Articles 20(1) and 22 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects shall be deemed to have been granted and made. An application for adjudication shall be filed within the implementation period of the improvement project for the relevant collapse risk area, notwithstanding Articles 23(1) and 28(1) of that Act. <Amended 2019.12.10>
③ Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects shall apply mutatis mutandis to expropriation or use under paragraph 1.

Chapter 5 Emergency Measures and Emergency Requisitions

Article 17 (Urgent Safety Measures for Disaster Prevention)
① Where a disaster has occurred or is likely to occur on a steep slope within the area under the jurisdiction of the head of a Si/Gun/Gu that has been found to pose a risk of collapse as a result of a safety inspection conducted under Article 5, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, order the interested persons to take safety measures, such as restricting or prohibiting use of the relevant facilities, repairing or reinforcing them, or removing them. In such cases, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall install signs near the steep slope indicating that a safety measure order has been issued and shall publish that fact in the local government's official gazette, on its website, or through similar means. <Amended 2017.3.21, 2024.2.13>
② When an interested person who has received a safety measure order under paragraph 1 implements the safety measures, that person shall notify the head of the Si/Gun/Gu of the results as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
③ Where a person who has received a safety measure order under paragraph 1 fails to comply, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu may take the necessary safety measures in that person's stead. In such cases, the Administrative Vicarious Execution Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 18 (Evacuation Orders) Where a disaster has occurred or is likely to occur in a collapse risk area, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may, if necessary to prevent danger to human life or bodily safety, issue an evacuation order, carry out compulsory evacuation, or take other such measures with respect to residents of the relevant area or persons present in the danger area.

Article 19 (Temporary Use of Land and Other Facilities)
① Where circumstances require emergency measures because a disaster has occurred or is likely to occur in a collapse risk area within his or her jurisdiction, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu may require persons at the disaster site or residing nearby to take emergency measures, or may, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, temporarily use another person's land, buildings, structures, or other property, or alter or remove obstacles. <Amended 2019.12.10>
② Where losses arise from emergency measures under paragraph 1, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall provide compensation in accordance with the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects.
③ Article 65 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety shall apply mutatis mutandis to medical treatment and compensation provided by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu for persons engaged in emergency measures pursuant to paragraph 1. <Amended 2017.3.21>

Chapter 6 Accumulation and Dissemination of Technologies for Disaster Prevention

Article 20 (Establishment of an Information System for Steep Slopes)
① When a person who has created a steep slope under any of the permits, authorizations, etc. issued pursuant to relevant statutes and regulations completes the relevant project, that person shall submit the completion documents to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction. <Amended 2017.3.21>
② A managing agency shall submit information on the current condition of a steep slope that it manages, including its specifications, photographs, and geotechnical investigation reports, to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the location of that slope. <Amended 2017.3.21>
③ The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall receive the completion documents, information on current conditions, and other materials under paragraphs 1 and 2, together with soil investigation data and other materials concerning construction projects at or above the scale prescribed by Presidential Decree that are carried out within his or her jurisdiction, establish a database, and provide the information to persons who need it. <Amended 2017.3.21>
④ The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall develop, disseminate, and operate the system necessary to establish the database under paragraphs 1 through 3, and shall prepare and distribute a nationwide geotechnical disaster risk map for use in various design and construction activities, prediction of collapse risks, and other purposes. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
⑤ Matters necessary for the completion documents and information on the current conditions of steep slopes submitted to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2017.3.21>

Article 21 (Standard Guidelines for Databases) To establish a system for providing comprehensive and unified information, the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall prepare standard guidelines for the integration and interoperability of the databases established under Article 20, and shall endeavor to accumulate and disseminate information and technologies concerning the safety management of steep slopes and disaster prevention. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 22 (Registration of Instrumentation Businesses)
① A person intending to engage in continuous instrumentation management as a business shall meet the registration requirements regarding technical capability, facilities, and other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, and shall register with the Mayor/Do Governor as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. The same shall apply where the person intends to change any registered matter prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2015.1.20, 2017.3.21, 2017.7.26, 2024.2.13>
② Where a person who has registered an instrumentation business pursuant to paragraph 1 (hereinafter referred to as an "instrumentation business operator") intends to close or suspend the business, the person shall report this to the Mayor/Do Governor as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2015.1.20, 2017.7.26>

Article 23 (Disqualifications of Instrumentation Business Operators) A person falling under any of the following shall not register an instrumentation business. <Amended 2017.3.21, 2021.1.12>
1. A person under adult guardianship;
2. A person sentenced to an unsuspended sentence of imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment for violating this Act, for whom 2 years have not elapsed since the execution of the sentence was completed (including cases where execution is deemed to have been completed) or remitted;
3. A person sentenced to imprisonment with labor for violating this Act, whose sentence has been suspended and who is still within the suspension period;
4. A person for whom 2 years have not elapsed since registration of the instrumentation business was revoked (excluding revocation on the ground specified in subparagraph 1);
5. A corporation with an officer falling under any of subparagraphs 1 through 4.

Article 24 (Succession to the Status of Instrumentation Business Operators)
① An instrumentation business operator intending to transfer or acquire the business of another instrumentation business operator, or to merge with a corporation that is another instrumentation business operator, shall report this to the Mayor/Do Governor as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2015.1.20>
② A transferee who has made a report pursuant to paragraph 1 and a corporation established through or surviving a merger shall respectively succeed to the status as an instrumentation business operator of the transferor and of the corporation before the merger.
③ Where an instrumentation business operator dies and the heir intends to succeed to that operator's status and engage in the instrumentation business, the heir shall report this to the Mayor/Do Governor as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2015.1.20>
④ The Mayor/Do Governor shall notify the reporting person of whether the report has been accepted within 14 days from receipt of a report under paragraph 1 or 3. <Newly inserted 2018.10.16>
⑤ Where the Mayor/Do Governor fails, within the period specified in paragraph 4, to notify the reporting person of acceptance or non-acceptance of the report, or of an extension of the processing period under the statutes and regulations governing the processing of civil petitions, the report shall be deemed to have been accepted on the day following the expiration of that period (meaning the relevant processing period where it has been extended or further extended under those statutes and regulations). <Newly inserted 2018.10.16>
⑥ Article 23 shall apply mutatis mutandis to reports under paragraphs 1 and 3. <Amended 2018.10.16>

Article 25 (Revocation of Registration of Instrumentation Businesses)
① Where an instrumentation business operator falls under any of the following, the Mayor/Do Governor may revoke the registration or order suspension of the business for a specified period not exceeding 3 months: Provided, That the registration shall be revoked in a case falling under subparagraph 1 or 3. <Amended 2015.1.20, 2017.3.21>
1. Where registration under Article 22 was obtained by false or fraudulent means;
2. Where the operator fails to meet the registration requirements under Article 22(1);
3. Where the operator comes to fall under any of the subparagraphs of Article 23: Provided, That this shall exclude a case in which, where an officer of a corporation falls under Article 23, subparagraph 5, that officer is replaced by a newly appointed officer within 3 months;
4. Where the operator lends the instrumentation business registration certificate or its name to another person, or subcontracts instrumentation work that it has contracted to undertake;
5. Where the operator prepares false measurement results, or prepares deficient measurement results intentionally or through gross negligence;
6. Where the operator fails to commence business for 2 years or longer after registration without just cause.
② The standards for administrative dispositions for each violation under paragraph 1 shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, taking into account the grounds for and severity of the violation. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 26 (Performance Inspections of Measurement Instruments)
① In undertaking continuous instrumentation management, an instrumentation business operator shall use measurement instruments that have passed a performance inspection conducted by the Minister of the Interior and Safety (hereinafter referred to as a "performance inspection"). <Amended 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
② Matters necessary for the subjects, standards, procedures, and other aspects of performance inspections shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
③ Where the results of a performance inspection under paragraph 2 are satisfactory, the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall issue an inspection certificate as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
④ The Minister of the Interior and Safety may have a person registered pursuant to Article 27 (hereinafter referred to as a "performance inspection agent") conduct performance inspections on the Minister's behalf. In such cases, where the results of a performance inspection under paragraph 2 are satisfactory, the performance inspection agent shall issue an inspection certificate as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 27 (Registration of Performance Inspection Agents)
① A person intending to act as an agent in conducting performance inspections shall meet the registration requirements regarding technical capability, facilities, and other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, and shall register with the Mayor/Do Governor. The same shall apply where the person intends to change any registered matter prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2015.1.20, 2017.7.26, 2020.2.18>
② A performance inspection agent may collect an inspection fee when conducting a performance inspection.
③ Article 24 shall apply mutatis mutandis to succession to the status of a performance inspection agent. In such cases, "instrumentation business operator" shall be construed as "performance inspection agent".

Article 28 (Disqualifications of Performance Inspection Agents) A person falling under any of the following shall not register as a performance inspection agent. <Amended 2017.3.21, 2021.1.12>
1. A person under adult guardianship;
2. A person sentenced to an unsuspended sentence of imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment for violating this Act, for whom 2 years have not elapsed since the execution of the sentence was completed (including cases where execution is deemed to have been completed) or remitted;
3. A person sentenced to imprisonment with labor for violating this Act, whose sentence has been suspended and who is still within the suspension period;
4. A person for whom 2 years have not elapsed since registration as a performance inspection agent was revoked (excluding revocation on the ground specified in subparagraph 1);
5. A corporation with an officer falling under any of subparagraphs 1 through 4.

Article 29 (Revocation of Registration of Performance Inspection Agents)
① Where a performance inspection agent falls under any of the following, the Mayor/Do Governor may revoke the registration or order suspension of the agent's duties for a specified period not exceeding 3 months: Provided, That the registration shall be revoked in a case falling under subparagraph 1 or 3. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2015.1.20, 2017.3.21, 2017.7.26, 2020.2.18>
1. Where registration under Article 27 was obtained by false or fraudulent means;
2. Where the agent fails to meet the registration requirements for agents under Article 27(1);
3. Where the agent comes to fall under any of the subparagraphs of Article 28: Provided, That this shall exclude a case in which, where an officer of a corporation falls under Article 28, subparagraph 5, that officer is replaced by a newly appointed officer within 3 months;
4. Where the agent lends the performance inspection agent registration certificate or its name to another person;
5. Where the agent prepares false performance inspection results or conducts a performance inspection by fraudulent means;
6. Where the agent refuses or evades a performance inspection without just cause.
② The standards for administrative dispositions for each violation under paragraph 1 shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, taking into account the grounds for and severity of the violation. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 30 (Prior Practical Training for Instrumentation Specialists)
① To ensure fairness and public confidence in continuous instrumentation management and to improve technical capabilities, the following persons shall complete in advance a practical education and training course conducted by the Minister of the Interior and Safety, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26, 2024.2.13>
1. A person performing continuous instrumentation management work pursuant to Article 8(1) (excluding cases in which such work is performed by another person on the person's behalf);
2. A specialist technician engaged in the instrumentation business pursuant to Article 22(1);
3. A specialist technician engaged in work as a performance inspection agent pursuant to Article 27(1).
② The Minister of the Interior and Safety may designate and publicly notify an institution or organization specializing in disaster prevention as an educational institution and have it provide the practical training under paragraph 1 on the Minister's behalf. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
③ The institution to which a person required to undergo the education and training under paragraph 1 belongs, or the employer employing that person, shall bear the expenses necessary for that person to receive the education and training. <Amended 2024.2.13>
④ Matters necessary for the requirements and procedures for designating educational institutions under paragraph 2 and other related matters shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 31 (Standards for Calculating Instrumentation Costs and Inspection Fees) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall prepare and publicly notify standards for calculating the costs of instrumentation used in continuous instrumentation management and the fees for performance inspections of measurement instruments, taking into account standard costs and other relevant factors. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 32 (Hearings) Where the Mayor/Do Governor intends to revoke registration of an instrumentation business or registration as a performance inspection agent, or to order suspension of business or duties pursuant to Article 25 or 29, the Mayor/Do Governor shall hold a hearing. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2015.1.20, 2017.7.26, 2020.2.18>

Article 32-2 (Establishment of the Korea Steep Slope Safety Association)
① The Korea Steep Slope Safety Association (hereinafter referred to as the "Association") may be established to support the promotion of research and information exchange concerning steep slopes and the strengthening of safety management for steep slopes.
② The Association shall be a juristic person.
③ The Association shall be formed upon registration of its establishment at the location of its principal office.
④ Membership of the Association shall consist of persons or organizations falling under any of the following:
1. Research organizations related to steep-slope safety management;
2. Persons prescribed by the articles of association who have extensive knowledge and experience concerning steep slopes;
3. Persons or organizations providing services, producing materials, carrying out construction, or undertaking other activities related to steep-slope safety management;
4. Other persons or organizations prescribed by the articles of association.
⑤ The duties of the Association shall be as follows:
1. Education and publicity to prevent steep-slope disasters and raise disaster prevention awareness;
2. Investigation, collection, and dissemination of materials concerning the prevention of steep-slope disasters, emergency disaster measures, disaster recovery, and related matters;
3. Publication of various materials concerning the prevention of steep-slope disasters, emergency disaster measures, disaster recovery, and related matters;
4. Promotion and support of relevant industries and development of technologies to advance technology in the field of steep slopes;
5. Attracting privately led domestic and international events related to steep-slope disasters;
6. Supporting the training of specialists in the field of steep slopes, and establishing and managing a personnel database;
7. Performing projects entrusted by the Government in the field of steep slopes;
8. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree concerning steep-slope safety management.

Article 32-3 (Articles of Association of the Association)
① Matters necessary for the contents of the Association's articles of association, the number and terms of office of its officers, the method of selecting officers, supervision, and other related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② The operating expenses of the Association shall be covered by membership fees and other business income.
③ Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated associations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Association.

Article 33 (Delegation of Authority or Entrustment of Duties)
① Part of the authority of the Minister of the Interior and Safety under this Act may be delegated to Mayors/Do Governors as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2014.11.19, 2015.1.20, 2017.7.26, 2024.2.13>
② Of the duties under this Act of the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayors, Do Governors, Special Self-Governing Province Governors, heads of Si/Gun/Gu, or managing agencies, the following may be entrusted to the Association as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly inserted 2024.2.13>
1. Safety inspections of steep slopes under Article 5;
2. Surveys of the actual conditions of steep slopes under Article 5-2(1);
3. Disaster risk assessments under Article 6(1) and (2);
4. Preparation and dissemination of documents and other materials concerning the standards for improvement projects for collapse risk areas under Article 13-2;
5. Establishment of databases under Article 20(3).

Article 33-2 (Performance of Duties by Agents)
① A managing agency may have a disaster prevention management measures agent under subparagraph 14 of Article 2 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as an "agent") perform, on its behalf, matters requiring specialist expertise, such as preliminary and feasibility investigations and analyses, and basic and detailed designs, among the following duties:
1. Safety inspections of steep slopes under Article 5;
2. Disaster risk assessments under Article 6;
3. Formulation of medium-term plans under Article 12;
4. Formulation of implementation plans for improvement projects for collapse risk areas under Article 13.
② Matters concerning the procedures and methods for selecting agents and other related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ Where a managing agency has an agent perform duties on its behalf, Article 38(2) and Articles 38-2 through 44 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the standards for calculating the cost of such agency work, grounds for disqualification from registration as an agent, requirements to be observed by agents, suspension or closure of operations, inspections of the actual conditions of agents, revocation of agents' registration, hearings, continuation of duties by agents whose registration has been revoked or whose duties have been suspended, and other related matters.

Chapter 7 Penalty Provisions

Article 34 (Penalty Provisions) A person falling under any of the following shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 2 years or by a fine not exceeding 20,000,000 won.
1. A person who engages in the business of continuous instrumentation management without registration under Article 22 or after registration has been revoked pursuant to Article 25;
2. A person who engages in the business of acting as a performance inspection agent without registration under Article 27 or after registration has been revoked pursuant to Article 29;
3. A person who obtains registration under Article 22 or 27 by false or fraudulent means.

Article 35 (Penalty Provisions) A person falling under any of the following shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 10,000,000 won. <Amended 2019.12.10>
1. A person who continues to perform work during a period of business suspension under Article 25;
2. A performance inspection agent under Article 26(4) who conducts a performance inspection fraudulently;
3. A person who continues to perform work during a period of suspension of duties under Article 29;
4. A person who performs duties as an agent without registration as an agent under Article 38(2) of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act, as applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 33-2(3).

Article 36 (Joint Penalty Provisions) Where the representative of a corporation, or an agent, employee, or other worker of a corporation or an individual commits a violation under Article 34 or 35 in connection with the business of that corporation or individual, the corporation or individual shall also be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant Article, in addition to punishment of the offender: Provided, That this shall not apply where the corporation or individual has not neglected due care and supervision concerning the relevant business to prevent the violation.

Article 37 (Administrative Fines)
① An administrative fine not exceeding 2,000,000 won shall be imposed on any of the following persons:
1. A person who damages instruments, equipment, or other items used for continuous instrumentation management under Article 8(4);
2. A person who moves or damages a hazard sign in violation of Article 11(3);
3. A person who fails to conduct his or her own safety inspection or to take necessary measures, such as emergency action, pursuant to Article 15(1);
4. A person who fails to comply with a safety measure order under Article 17(1);
5. A person who refuses to comply with an evacuation order or other such order under Article 18;
6. A person who refuses or obstructs the temporary use of land, buildings, or other property, or the alteration or removal of obstacles under Article 19;
7. A person who fails to submit completion documents relating to a steep slope pursuant to Article 20(1);
8. A person who fails to report the transfer or acquisition of an instrumentation business or other related matters, in violation of Article 24(1) and (3) (including where those provisions apply mutatis mutandis under Article 27(3)).
② The administrative fines under paragraph 1 shall be imposed and collected by the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2020.2.18>
